Subject: Model output missing keys in batch responses

Hi Tessa,

We're seeing intermittent missing fields in the JSON payloads when we run batched generation against the Redwood hosted API. Specifically, our pipeline expects a top-level "summary" key in each item, but ~1-2% of items come back without that key (the rest of the object is present). This started happening after we moved to the v1 streaming SDK and also began sending larger batch sizes (up to 16).

I've attached a small sample of the responses we captured (brightline_sample_resp.json) plus the request metadata. Example: one response object was {"id":"abc", "text":"..."} — no "summary" field. We rely on that key for downstream enrichment, so it's causing processing errors.

Can you confirm if this is a platform issue? Happy to share request IDs or live logs.

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: RE: Model output missing keys in batch responses — investigation notes

Hi all,

I ran reproductions against the hosted runtime and the dedicated test pool using the request pattern and payloads Alex shared. Summary of findings:

- Test matrix: batch sizes 1/4/8/16, streaming vs non-streaming, SDK versions 1.3.7 and 1.4.2-rc.
- Observed behavior: We could not reproduce missing top-level keys from the server side. All server responses contain the expected JSON schema.
- Root cause hypothesis: a client-side parsing race when using the streaming SDK. In our tests, when the client parses partial chunks as separate JSON objects before the final chunk arrives, a malformed/incomplete parse path in the Brightline parser led to silently dropping optional keys like "summary" for that item. This surface-level drop looks identical to a missing-key server response.

Evidence: attached investigation log (redwood_investigation_log.txt) includes raw server payloads and the full chunk boundaries we sent. Each complete response from the server contains the "summary" key. The logs show the client received three chunks for one item: chunk A (prefix), chunk B (body including "summary"), chunk C (suffix). If the client concatenates only A+C by accident (race), the "summary" text can be lost before JSON parse.

Action items we recommend (workarounds):
1) Upgrade to redwood-sdk@1.4.2 (released as stable today) which includes a small buffering debounce for streaming parsers.
2) If you manage your own streaming parse loop, ensure you assemble chunks until a full JSON object terminator ("}") is observed or use a streaming JSON parser that handles partial objects robustly.

We've opened a tracking issue on our SDK repo to improve examples and add a small defensive guard for SDK users: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/234

Let us know if you want us to run a short session to observe Brightline's parser. We are ready to test any updated client code you push.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Model output missing keys in batch responses — closure

Hi Alex,

Following Marcus's investigation and the workaround steps, Sophie and your engineering team confirmed this morning that upgrading to redwood-sdk@1.4.2 and adding a short chunk-assembly debounce resolved the missing-key occurrences. Brightline observed zero missing "summary" keys across a 24-hour 100k-item run after the change.

We're marking this incident closed on the Redwood side since server-side logs show all responses were valid and the issue was due to client parsing of streaming chunks. Apologies for the time lost — we've also prioritized improving the SDK docs and adding an example that demonstrates safe streaming JSON assembly.

If you'd like, Marcus can schedule a 30-minute pairing session to review your parser and confirm robustness across edge cases.

Thanks again for reporting and working through this with us. Please re-open the thread or file a new one if anything else appears.

Best,
